transcript: I don't think y'all are ready for batboy at City Center. That was the most insane show I've ever seen, in the best way. I was at the invited dress tonight, so we were the very first audience to see this version of the show. And for me, it was completely new because I've actually never seen batboy before. It's a show that I've always been tangentially familiar with, and I know a lot of people really love it, but I just never got around to listening to it. So I can't speak to how this new version compares to the original, although I do know that they made pretty significant changes, including a bunch of new songs and a reworked book. But I will say that this version, I think, is something really special. It's hard for me to think of a better match in material and director than batboy and Alex Timbers. Alex Timbers being the visionary director behind Beetlejuice, Moulin Rouge, here lies love. I think that Alex really understands the tone of the show, which, yes, is quirky and absurd, but also has a heart at the center of it. I think that Alex really finds the perfect balance. I also think of all of the City Center productions I've seen, this one is by far the most polished. There is nary a binder in sight. Pretty much everyone is off book. There's an actual set by David Corens. It is incredibly simple, but also very Effective and really elevated by some incredible lighting by Justin Townsend. That really makes this feel like more than just a concert. I really do think that you could more or less plop this on a Broadway stage and it would be ready to go. And the cast is not only stacked, but everyone feels so perfectly cast in their roles. You have so many heavy hitters like Carrie Butler, who was in the original production, Chris Seabourne, Andrew Durand and Alex Noel in the Perfect Princess track. They just come on, belt their face off, and leave and completely steal the show. And it is, of course, LED by Taylor Trench, who is playing the titular bat boy, which in many ways feels like the role that he was born to play. Without giving away too much, it's an incredibly physically demanding role that requires so much out of him, and he's able to play all of the different facets of this character really well. I really cannot say enough good things about this production. And I'll also say, if you know nothing about batboy, go in blind. Just enjoy the journey, because there are so many fun twists and turns in the show. There was a lot of gasps in our audience at various revelations, so that's my recommendation. But honestly, even if you know the show, I still think you'll have a great time. And there still may even be a surprise or two for you along The way
